government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experimental Evidence From China
government.short_title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experime…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how people's beliefs about corruption influence their attitudes towards fighting it. In a large survey experiment conducted in China, researchers found that when people were told the actual level of tolerance for corruption is much lower than they thought, it made them more likely to want to fight corruption. However, if this information was paired with suggestions of punishment, it seemed to weaken the effect. This shows that simply telling people about how corrupt others are might not be as effective as also showing what actions can be taken against it.

government.title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Public Rights
government.short_title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Pu…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments in Iran handle situations where their actions harm collective interests or public rights. It examines legal systems that provide ways to compensate for such harms and restore balance. The research finds there are different types of compensation depending on whether the government acted wrongfully or not, and it also covers cases where they did something lawful but still caused damage. Challenges like unclear laws, difficulty proving harm in collective situations, and lack of coordination between different parts of the system can make these mechanisms less effective even if the basic rules are clear.

government.title: The Legal Foundations for the Evolving Role of Oversight Bodies in Combating Corruption in Iraq
government.short_title: The Legal Foundations for the Evolving Role of Oversight Bodies in Combating Corruption in Iraq
government.source: Interdisciplinary Studies in Society, Law, and Politics
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how the legal system in Iraq supports oversight bodies in fighting corruption. It examines the laws and constitution that give these bodies their powers and how they've grown stronger over time. The study also looks at international agreements that have influenced Iraq's approach. The main goal is to make sure these bodies can effectively monitor and prevent corruption.

government.title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption in Afghanistan during the Republican Period (2004–2021)
government.short_title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: During the Republican period in Afghanistan (2004-2021), administrative corruption was a major issue affecting governance. The government worked with international support to create laws, anti-corruption strategies, and institutions. However, despite progress in these areas, corruption did not significantly decrease. The study found that while there were improvements in legislation and institution building, the effectiveness of policies weakened at implementation stages.

government.title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Official Channels: A Critical Analysis of the 2013 Anti‑Smuggling Law and Its 2021 Amendments
government.short_title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Of…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The smuggling of goods and currency through official channels in Iran remains a significant issue despite various laws enacted over the years. While there have been efforts like the 2013 Anti-Smuggling Law and subsequent amendments, this practice has not decreased but may have worsened in some areas such as reverse smuggling and organized currency trafficking. This article examines how well these laws balance different goals like prevention, repression, rehabilitation, and compensation. It found that while there are positive changes, the law still faces major issues including a broad definition of smuggling, multiple bodies leading to lengthy proceedings, disproportionate penalties, and weak enforcement due to corruption.

government.title: Medicine between ethics and politics: a historical and bioethical interpretation of the Russian medical tradition
government.short_title: Medicine between ethics and politics: a historical and bioethical interpretation of the Russia…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses a book about the history of medicine in Russia, focusing on how ethics and politics have influenced medical practices. The book covers how medical ethics, deontology, and bioethics have developed within the context of public policy, social changes, and international relations. It emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary research and highlights how understanding these aspects can help us better grasp the Russian medical tradition. The practical implication is that this knowledge can inform current and future medical practices and policies in Russia.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities of Nigeria
government.short_title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities…
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) was implemented in 2015 to centralize public funds and improve transparency and accountability in Nigerian federal universities, but financial irregularities still occur. This study found that TSA has improved transparency and accountability significantly (p=0.004), but also faces challenges like bureaucratic delays and actors circumventing the system. Corruption persists as it transforms into less traceable forms. Despite savings of over 10 trillion Naira nationally, corruption perception scores remain low.

government.title: Behavioral Orientations and Self-Rated Performance Among University Employees in Vietnam
government.short_title: Behavioral Orientations and Self-Rated Performance Among University Employees in Vietnam
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how university employees in Vietnam feel about their work and how they perform. It examined five behaviors: responsibility, discipline, engagement, cooperation, and adaptability. These behaviors were connected to four areas of performance, like how well they handle their tasks and how they get along with others. The study found that adaptability and cooperation were most strongly linked to all areas of performance.

government.short_title: Control of corruption in Emerging Asian Economies: The influence of GDP, freedom and speech, r…

government.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
government.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
government.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
government.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

government.title: The ‘formidable inspector’: visual imagery, transparency, and the critique of government corruption in <italic>A Picture of the Treasury</italic>
government.short_title: The ‘formidable inspector’: visual imagery, transparency, and the critique of government corru…
government.plain_summary: In his work "A Picture of the Treasury," Jeremy Bentham used visual imagery to expose corruption within the government. He argued that transparency is crucial for preventing misconduct and misrule, and he applied this idea through the concept of the inspection principle. This principle suggests that the public should have access to information about how institutions operate, allowing them to hold officials accountable. Bentham's "Picture" portrays him as a "formidable inspector," highlighting a conspiracy to hide corruption and advocating for public scrutiny.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.short_title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.plain_summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are harmful chemicals found in many products that have contaminated the environment. The US government has not uniformly addressed PFAS issues, but some states like Maine have taken strong actions. Maine has implemented various measures such as education, labeling requirements, and bans on certain agricultural practices. They also have unique regulations like banning the use of PFAS in food products like beef, dairy, and eggs.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Technology is Advancing Every Day, We Think Oversight Should Too!
government.short_title: Technology is Advancing Every Day, We Think Oversight Should Too!

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Market Failure or Government Failure? A Response to Jaworski
government.short_title: Market Failure or Government Failure? A Response to Jaworski

government.title: Building Integrity in the Global South: Lessons from Pakistan’s Struggle Against Public Sector Corruption
government.short_title: Building Integrity in the Global South: Lessons from Pakistan’s Struggle Against Public Sector…

government.title: CRIMINAL SANCTIONS FOR SOCIAL WORK FOR PERPETRATORS OF CORRUPTION Law
government.short_title: CRIMINAL SANCTIONS FOR SOCIAL WORK FOR PERPETRATORS OF CORRUPTION Law
government.source: Dusturiyah: Jurnal Hukum Islam, Perundang-undangan dan Pranata Sosial
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how community service is used as a punishment for people who do bad things like corruption. It found that community service helps both the person who did wrong and society by helping them learn and change. From Islamic law, this is seen as a good way to help offenders and keep society safe. But it's not enough on its own; it needs to be used with other punishments too.

government.title: Corruption pathways and governance failures in Thailand’s public construction projects: Phases, mechanisms, and stakeholders
government.short_title: Corruption pathways and governance failures in Thailand’s public construction projects: Phases…
government.plain_summary: This study examines corruption in Thailand's public construction projects, looking at seven main ways corruption happens across all phases of a project. It found that corruption is most common during the planning, bidding, and execution stages. The study also shows that corruption is supported by interactions among government officials, contractors, and other stakeholders. It suggests that to prevent corruption, it's important to address issues like government transparency, fair bidding processes, and better oversight.

government.title: AN INVESTIGATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE CODE OF CONDUCT BUREAU IN COMBATING ADMINISTRATIVE CORRUPTION IN NIGERIA
government.short_title: AN INVESTIGATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE CODE OF CONDUCT BUREAU IN COMBATING ADMINISTRATIV…
government.source: FUGUS Journal of Public Administration and Management
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how well the Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB) in Nigeria is doing in fighting corruption among public officials. The CCB helps people declare their assets and promotes good behavior. It also investigates when people break the rules. The study found that the CCB has helped people declare their assets and improved ethical standards, but it faces challenges like not having enough money, weak systems, and political interference.

government.title: When Geography Dilutes Accountability: Managerial Discretion and Fiscal Expansion in Local Government
government.short_title: When Geography Dilutes Accountability: Managerial Discretion and Fiscal Expansion in Local Gov…
government.source: The American Review of Public Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how local governments manage their finances and how they are accountable to voters. When a city relies on taxes that affect people who don't live there, like commuters or travelers, it's harder for those who pay the taxes to hold the government accountable. The research found that cities that can shift some of these costs to nonvoters end up spending more money. This happens more in cities near big areas with lots of traffic.

government.title: Negotiating power and trust: digital government communication in India’s risk-driven networked public sphere
government.short_title: Negotiating power and trust: digital government communication in India’s risk-driven networked…
government.source: Journal of Information, Communication and Ethics in Society
government.plain_summary: This study examines how Indian government officials use digital communication to engage citizens, build trust, and manage crises. It found a model where the government's digital power is balanced by publics and systemic risks. Despite efforts to improve efficiency and legitimacy, there are ongoing tensions between control and dialogue, and between using digital tools for governance and fostering genuine responsiveness. This research provides a new model called negotiated digital governmentality to explain how digital practices shape policy and citizen involvement in Indian democracy.

government.title: Thermodynamic analysis of charged anti-de Sitter black holes with cloud of strings in Einstein-bumblebee gravity via Bekenstein–Hawking and Tsallis entropies
government.short_title: Thermodynamic analysis of charged anti-de Sitter black holes with cloud of strings in Einstein…
government.source: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Science
government.plain_summary: This study examines the thermodynamics of black holes in a special type of gravity called Einstein-bumblebee gravity. These black holes have a cloud of strings surrounding them. The researchers looked at how the temperature, energy, and other properties of these black holes change. They found that the presence of the string cloud and the special gravity can cause the black hole to behave differently, with a phase transition similar to how water turns into ice.

government.title: Rule of Law or Rule of Politics? Understanding Varieties of Judicial Anti-Corruption Campaigns
government.short_title: Rule of Law or Rule of Politics? Understanding Varieties of Judicial Anti-Corruption Campaigns
government.source: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
government.plain_summary: This study looks at anti-corruption efforts by judges and prosecutors targeting powerful politicians. It finds these campaigns are often political moves rather than purely legal actions. They can either strengthen fair governance or just look good without changing anything real. The effectiveness varies widely depending on how open the process is, what kind of government they're in, and if it leads to less corruption or other problems like people losing trust in leaders.

government.title: Transparency, Corruption, and Trust in Determining Residents’ Support for the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL): A Longitudinal Study
government.short_title: Transparency, Corruption, and Trust in Determining Residents’ Support for the Bangladesh Premi…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how transparency and corruption affect people's support for a sports league in Bangladesh. It found that when events are transparent, people trust the government and organizers more. But when people think there's corruption, their trust goes down. People also feel better about their lives when they think the event will bring benefits to their area.

government.title: Govern, Map, Measure, Absorb: The Legibility Trap in Public Sector Participatory AI Governance
government.short_title: Govern, Map, Measure, Absorb: The Legibility Trap in Public Sector Participatory AI Governance
government.source: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how public sector agencies use participatory design to prevent algorithmic harm, but often overlooks real community input that could limit state power. The authors introduce the concept of the "legibility trap," where institutions document participation in ways that only show inputs that fit their categories, excluding dissent and demands for not using systems. This trap is similar to how states simplify complex situations to control information. The study analyzed documents from three AI projects and found that participation is often filtered to avoid challenging state power.

government.title: From Visibility to Accountability: Designing Actionable Transparency Infrastructures for Public-Sector AI
government.short_title: From Visibility to Accountability: Designing Actionable Transparency Infrastructures for Publi…
government.source: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
government.plain_summary: Transparency in AI systems for public sector has become important, but it often just gives people information about AI systems without allowing them to hold the government accountable. This can be seen in things like algorithmic registers where details about AI systems are available, but they don't easily help civil society or the media check on how the government is using AI. Our research found that these registers often have issues like data being split up in different places, making it hard to compare information, and not having ways for the public to easily use the data. To fix this, we created design principles and a prototype platform called PublicAlgo that aims to make it easier for the public to use the information provided by these registers.

government.title: DIGITAL GOVERNANCE AND TRANSPARENCY: LEVERAGING E-GOVERNMENT SYSTEMS TO COMBAT CORRUPTION IN SOUTH AFRICA
government.short_title: DIGITAL GOVERNANCE AND TRANSPARENCY: LEVERAGING E-GOVERNMENT SYSTEMS TO COMBAT CORRUPTION IN S…
government.plain_summary: Digital governance is crucial for reducing corruption in South Africa. E-government systems, like open government data, digital service platforms, and e-procurement, enhance transparency by making public processes more visible, standardized, and auditable. This helps reduce opportunities for bribery and rent-seeking by limiting face-to-face interactions and constraining decision-making. However, these benefits are not automatic; factors like weak institutional capacity, uneven digital infrastructure, and limited data usability can undermine their effectiveness.

government.title: Visible integrity in public leadership: a conceptual model of truth-telling and accountability
government.short_title: Visible integrity in public leadership: a conceptual model of truth-telling and accountability
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a model for visible integrity in public leadership, focusing on how senior officials can maintain honesty and accountability in their work. It explores how they can tell the truth even when it's difficult, like when they face pressure from their boss or when they're unsure about the right thing to do. The model includes five key areas: being honest under pressure, showing clear ethical behavior, limiting their own actions when necessary, and holding their institution accountable to the public. The study also introduces a concept from Indonesia called jiwa ketok, which helps explain how public officials can be transparent about their actions.

government.title: Government Capability, Benevolence, and Public Trust in Cyber Risk Governance: Evidence from a Survey Experiment on Telecom Fraud in China
government.short_title: Government Capability, Benevolence, and Public Trust in Cyber Risk Governance: Evidence from a…
government.plain_summary: This study investigates how government capability and benevolence influence public trust in cyber risk governance. It used a survey experiment with 683 participants, manipulating government capability and benevolence as high or low, and varying the risk scenario between low and high. The results showed that government capability had a stronger impact on trust than benevolence. When both were high, trust increased.

government.title: Ethical Foundations of Anti-Corruption in the Civil Service System of the People’s Republic of China
government.short_title: Ethical Foundations of Anti-Corruption in the Civil Service System of the People’s Republic of…
government.plain_summary: This summary explains the ethical foundations of anti-corruption in China's civil service system. Unlike many countries that rely solely on formal laws, China uses a combination of official virtue shaped by Confucian tradition and socialist ideology. This approach balances party discipline with legal responsibility. The Chinese model shows how ethical principles are integrated into a system that includes traditional values, ideology, and centralized control.

government.title: <b>Government Accounting Reform and Public Accountability: A Systematic Review of Themes, Methods, and Institutional Conditions</b>
government.short_title: <b>Government Accounting Reform and Public Accountability: A Systematic Review of Themes…
government.source: International Journal of Management, Economic and Accounting
government.plain_summary: This study looks at government accounting reforms and how they affect public financial information. It found that while adopting new accounting standards like IPSAS can make financial information more transparent, this doesn't always lead to better governance. The key is how these reforms are implemented and how they fit with the existing institutions. For example, if the government doesn't have the right skills or if the audits aren't thorough, the new accounting standards won't work as well.

government.title: Treasury Single Account and Transparency and Accountability in Public Fund Management: Evidence from Ministries, Departments and Agencies in Osun State, Nigeria
government.short_title: Treasury Single Account and Transparency and Accountability in Public Fund Management: Evidenc…
government.source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) is a financial management reform that consolidates government revenue collection and management into one account. This consolidation improves transparency and accountability in public fund management by making government financial transactions more visible and easier to monitor. It reduces opportunities for unauthorized control of public resources and enhances access to information. In Osun State, Nigeria, the TSA implementation has led to improved transparency and accountability in public fund management, as evidenced by better monitoring and reduced misuse of funds.

government.title: A Study on Community Anti-Fraud Practice for the Elderly from the Perspective of Technology-Service Coupling-A Case Study of the “Private-Domain Eagle Eye” APP
government.short_title: A Study on Community Anti-Fraud Practice for the Elderly from the Perspective of Technology-Se…
government.source: Journal of Modern Education and Culture
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how to prevent fraud targeting the elderly, especially in digital social groups like WeChat. As more seniors use the internet, they become vulnerable to scams like fake health products or financial schemes. Traditional ways of stopping fraud, like lectures, aren't enough because they can't keep up with the quick changes in scams. The study introduces a new method called "technology-service coupling" where smart tools help spot scams, but human workers follow up to stop them.

government.title: International Human Rights Law and Anti-LGBTQ+ Legislation in Africa: Assessing the Effectiveness of International Anti-Discrimination Norms in Comparative Perspective
government.short_title: International Human Rights Law and Anti-LGBTQ+ Legislation in Africa: Assessing the Effectiven…
government.source: International Social Sciences and Education Journal
government.plain_summary: This study examines how international human rights laws and anti-discrimination norms work in African countries, especially regarding laws that discriminate against LGBTQ+ individuals. It finds that while these international standards provide a strong legal foundation to protect people from discrimination, their effectiveness varies. States often resist these norms, either through their own laws or by prioritizing religious or cultural values. However, when domestic courts, regional bodies, and civil society groups actively push for these international standards, it can lead to better protections for LGBTQ+ people.

government.title: Ethical Orientation: Key to the Sustenance of the Fight Against Corruption in the Power Sector in Nigeria
government.short_title: Ethical Orientation: Key to the Sustenance of the Fight Against Corruption in the Power Sector…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how corruption is a significant issue in Nigeria's power sector, affecting economic development. Despite efforts, nearly 87 million Nigerians still lack electricity. The study suggests that promoting ethical behavior could help combat corruption. It proposes that all sectors, including the power sector, should follow codes of ethics.

government.title: Examining Transparency and Accountability Mechanisms in Public Sector Management
government.short_title: Examining Transparency and Accountability Mechanisms in Public Sector Management
government.source: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management and Social Science
government.plain_summary: Transparency and accountability are crucial for improving how public sector organizations operate. They help build public trust and enhance the effectiveness of services provided. This study found that both transparency and accountability positively impact public sector management, with accountability having a stronger influence. To improve, public sector organizations need to enhance how they disclose information and strengthen accountability measures like reporting, oversight, and performance evaluations.

government.title: Reengineering trust: E-public procurement and government transparency
government.short_title: Reengineering trust: E-public procurement and government transparency
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how e-procurement, which is using digital technology for buying goods and services, can help make government buying more fair, transparent, and honest. It shows that e-procurement can reduce opportunities for corruption by limiting direct contact between officials and contractors. However, it also points out that there are challenges like not having enough technology or support from institutions. The main idea is that while e-procurement is important, it needs to be supported by fixing these issues to work well.

government.title: Corrigendum to “The effects of education on corruption: Evidence from Vietnam’s university expansion” [J. Public Econ. 262 (2026) 105763]
government.short_title: Corrigendum to “The effects of education on corruption: Evidence from Vietnam’s university exp…

government.title: Ownership and efficiency in municipal waste management: evidence from a fragmented local government system
government.short_title: Ownership and efficiency in municipal waste management: evidence from a fragmented local gover…
government.source: International Journal of Public Sector Management
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the ownership of waste collection providers affects the efficiency of municipal waste management in Croatia. It uses a two-stage analysis, first looking at cost and environmental service efficiency, and then examining the relationship between ownership types and these efficiencies while controlling for other factors. The findings suggest that having internal ownership, where the municipality owns the waste collection company, is not associated with efficiency. However, mixed ownership, where the municipality and other public entities share ownership, is negatively related to cost efficiency.

government.title: Electronic Governance and Transparency at the Local Government Level: The Role of Research
government.short_title: Electronic Governance and Transparency at the Local Government Level: The Role of Research
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how local governments can use technology to be more transparent and efficient. With advancements in technology, local governments can reduce costs by not needing physical offices and less paper. However, the study also found that not everyone is literate enough to use these technologies, and governments need to provide the necessary infrastructure. The study suggests that there needs to be strong support from leaders and government should allocate funds to make e-governance work effectively.

government.title: Digital transformation in e-government services: exploring the role of public trust, transparency, accountability and citizen satisfaction in real-time service delivery
government.short_title: Digital transformation in e-government services: exploring the role of public trust, transpare…
government.source: Journal of Science and Technology Policy Management
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how e-government services can be improved by making them more transparent, accountable, and trusted. It found that when people believe the government is open and honest about what it does, and that it follows rules fairly, they are more likely to use these services. The study also shows that if people feel their efforts are worth it and that the service helps them, they are more likely to use it. This research helps governments create better e-government services by making them more transparent and accountable, which in turn makes people more willing to use them.

government.plain_summary: This study looked at how anti-corruption agencies worked to reduce corruption in Adamawa State, Nigeria. They used surveys to gather data from 380 people. The study found that having good policies and strong structures helps create effective strategies to fight corruption. Collaboration among different groups also plays a big role in making these strategies work.

government.title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector digital development
government.short_title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector dig…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public sector organizations can better govern digital development projects. It suggests that instead of relying on existing tools, digital solutions should be designed to make governance more visible, comparable, and subject to collective decision-making. The research found that by actively specifying governance through design, digital solutions can lead to more transparent discussions and decisions. However, long-term outcomes like strategic alignment and public value creation are harder to measure.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relations
nonprofit.short_title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relat…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: The new middle class in Iran grew significantly after the Islamic Revolution and played a key role in pushing for reforms in both domestic and foreign policies. This group became more active in elections over time, aiming to influence how the government handled these areas. Despite their efforts through voting, they haven't been able to fully change the system's approach to politics internationally or domestically. Their success was mainly seen in getting more people involved in electoral processes.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
nonprofit.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
nonprofit.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

nonprofit.title: From Visibility to Accountability: Designing Actionable Transparency Infrastructures for Public-Sector AI
nonprofit.short_title: From Visibility to Accountability: Designing Actionable Transparency Infrastructures for Publi…
nonprofit.source: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
nonprofit.plain_summary: Transparency in AI systems for public sector has become important, but it often just gives people information about AI systems without allowing them to hold the government accountable. This can be seen in things like algorithmic registers where details about AI systems are available, but they don't easily help civil society or the media check on how the government is using AI. Our research found that these registers often have issues like data being split up in different places, making it hard to compare information, and not having ways for the public to easily use the data. To fix this, we created design principles and a prototype platform called PublicAlgo that aims to make it easier for the public to use the information provided by these registers.

nonprofit.title: International Human Rights Law and Anti-LGBTQ+ Legislation in Africa: Assessing the Effectiveness of International Anti-Discrimination Norms in Comparative Perspective
nonprofit.short_title: International Human Rights Law and Anti-LGBTQ+ Legislation in Africa: Assessing the Effectiven…
nonprofit.source: International Social Sciences and Education Journal
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study examines how international human rights laws and anti-discrimination norms work in African countries, especially regarding laws that discriminate against LGBTQ+ individuals. It finds that while these international standards provide a strong legal foundation to protect people from discrimination, their effectiveness varies. States often resist these norms, either through their own laws or by prioritizing religious or cultural values. However, when domestic courts, regional bodies, and civil society groups actively push for these international standards, it can lead to better protections for LGBTQ+ people.

nonprofit.title: The Accountability Architecture: Linking Robust Financial Controls to Institutional Advancement in the NGO Sector
nonprofit.short_title: The Accountability Architecture: Linking Robust Financial Controls to Institutional Advancemen…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how strong financial controls affect the growth of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in East Africa. It found that having good financial controls, especially strong internal systems, helps NGOs grow. The research used surveys and interviews to gather data. The key takeaway is that NGOs need to focus on their financial controls to grow and be successful.
